decisions.reason: As a recently launched camera in the firm’s core space-optics business, it should be kept because market uncertainty is still high in long space procurement cycles and the cost of extending this option is likely modest for a large R&D-intensive firm.

The modular space navigation camera fits the firm’s move toward flexible and reprogrammable systems, so management would keep the option open while customers and missions reveal its value over more than a single launch year.

The space situational awareness sensor suite builds on established capabilities and addresses a strategically relevant application area, so with little negative evidence so far it is rational to continue rather than abandon early.

Although it appears less prominently marketed, the miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor matches the firm’s direction toward compact sensors for future spacecraft and small satellites, making it worth retaining while its commercial potential becomes clearer.
